_meta.note: Recent foreign-policy posture for game relations. Scores -2 hostile .. 2 close ally, reflecting current governments (2025-2026). Each score/pair/event has a dated source URL. Game effects built on this are illustrative.
_meta.method: Two web-research passes (Asia-Pacific/Americas; Europe/Middle East/Africa), merged without new judgement; UNVERIFIED items excluded.
_meta.spotChecked: 2026-11-01: China draft AI export list (Oct 16; 23 AI items of ~40), Qatar/UAE Pax Silica (Jan 12/14), EU AI Act omnibus (high-risk to Dec 2027), Colombia inauguration (Aug 7) re-verified by Tuba's session; weak sources swapped for official/legal ones.
_meta.euMembers: Two EU member states count as +1 (shared EU membership) when no sourced bilateral pair exists.

US.name: United States
US.summary: Tariff-heavy unilateralism; managed truce with China while selectively loosening AI-chip sales; pressing allies for investment and export-control alignment.

basis.claim: Xi state visit to Washington produced short truce extension to Jan 10, 2027, AI talks; no chip or Taiwan breakthrough.
Section 301 forced-labor tariffs of 10% or 12.5% imposed on 60 economies, including China and most US partners.
During Trump's Beijing visit, US approved Nvidia H200 licences for Chinese buyers; Beijing reportedly discouraged purchases.
Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs; administration shifted to Section 122 surcharge, then Section 301/232 tools.
Section 232 proclamation set 25% tariff on certain advanced chips, inviting country deals for relief.

CN.name: China
CN.summary: Uses rare-earth and dual-use export controls as leverage; truce with US, coercion of Japan, courts Korea, India, Canada and ASEAN.

basis.claim: China published draft catalogue of ~40 AI, chip, solar and biotech technologies for export restriction; comments due Nov 15.
China put MP Materials, USA Rare Earth and eight other US firms on its export-control list.
MOFCOM banned dual-use exports to Japanese military end-users after Takaichi's Taiwan remarks; rare earths affected.
EU and China reportedly reached preliminary deal on rare-earth licences and EV import limits amid wider tensions.

JP.name: Japan
JP.summary: Firmly US-aligned under Takaichi; deep freeze with China over Taiwan remarks and export curbs; steady shuttle diplomacy with Korea.

basis.claim: Takaichi called China an 'important neighbour' but vowed to firmly assert Japan's positions amid deep freeze.
Takaichi met Trump in New York, touting $550bn US investment pledge and defence build-up.
China added Japanese entities to dual-use Control and Watch lists, escalating January export ban.
Takaichi visited Andong for third Lee-Takaichi summit; supply-chain and critical-minerals cooperation stressed.

TW.name: Taiwan
TW.summary: Locked into US tech alignment via $250bn chip investment deal and export-control alignment; under steady PRC military pressure.

basis.claim: US-Taiwan deal: $250bn chip investment plus $250bn credit guarantees; US reciprocal tariff capped at 15%.
Agreement on Reciprocal Trade signed; Taiwan to align chip export controls with US Foreign Direct Product Rule.
China held live-fire drills around Taiwan after record $11bn US arms sale.
China ran coastal live-fire drills after Lai's National Day speech, accusing him of seeking independence.

KR.name: South Korea
KR.summary: Lee balances: US ally straining over $350bn investment terms and tariffs, while pursuing 'full restoration' with China and stable Japan ties.

basis.claim: Lee said $350bn US investment deal talks cause 'sleepless nights'; parts reopened after near-final draft.
National Assembly passed bill enabling $350bn US investment to ease tariffs after Trump threatened 25%.
Lee held state visit summit with Xi in Beijing, seeking full restoration of ties in 2026.

SG.name: Singapore
SG.summary: Open-economy hedger: no retaliation against US tariffs, enforces US chip-smuggling cases, keeps close China economic ties.

basis.claim: PM Wong said Singapore still awaiting US chip sectoral tariff outcome; 'cannot afford to turn inwards'.
Singapore police seized $42m bungalow in Nvidia server smuggling probe linked to diversion to China.
US reportedly probing Singapore-based Apex Logistics over alleged Nvidia AI chip smuggling to China (anonymous sources).

IN.name: India
IN.summary: Multi-aligned: joined US Pax Silica tech pact but US trade deal unsigned and Russian-oil tariff threat; cautious thaw with China; EU FTA concluded.

basis.claim: Modi and Xi met on BRICS sidelines in New Delhi; Xi's first India visit since 2019, 'partners not rivals'.
Trump signed sanctions law allowing up to 100% tariffs on top Russian-energy buyers including India and China.
US-India interim trade framework: 18% reciprocal rate; 25% Russian-oil penalty dropped; final deal still unsigned.
India signed US-led Pax Silica declaration on secure AI and semiconductor supply chains.
EU and India concluded free trade agreement after nearly two decades of talks.

ID.name: Indonesia
ID.summary: Prabowo hedges: signed US trade deal with mineral and third-country clauses, defence pact; nickel industry still China-built.

basis.claim: US-Indonesia reciprocal trade deal finalised: 19% tariff, critical-mineral export access, third-country alignment clause.
Analysis: Indonesia-China partnership more fragile than it appears as US deal tests Chinese-built nickel ecosystem.
Indonesia placed in lower 10% tier of US Section 301 forced-labor tariffs.

MY.name: Malaysia
MY.summary: Formally aligned with US export controls via 2025 trade pact, yet weighing Huawei Ascend chips for sovereign AI; classic hedger.

basis.claim: Malaysia weighing Huawei Ascend 910C for sovereign AI project despite US warnings; US trade pact unratified.
MITI imposed permit requirement on export/transshipment of US-origin high-performance AI chips.

TH.name: Thailand
TH.summary: Anutin government near US tariff deal (~19%) but slow; closer to China; Cambodia border dispute strained US mediation.

basis.claim: Thai PM says US trade agreement close to completion; signing targeted around November summits.
US paused trade talks over Cambodia peace deal suspension; Thailand insisted tracks be separated.
Thailand placed in higher 12.5% tier of US Section 301 tariffs.

VN.name: Vietnam
VN.summary: Bamboo diplomacy: warm party-to-party ties with Beijing, rail deals; US trade deal still unsigned over transshipment.

basis.claim: To Lam's four-day state visit to China yielded 32 agreements incl. border-Haiphong rail feasibility study.
To Lam said Vietnam 'very close' to US trade deal, denied rerouting Chinese goods.
Vietnam placed in 12.5% tier of US Section 301 tariffs.

AU.name: Australia
AU.summary: Close US ally (AUKUS, minerals pact) while keeping a stabilised but tense trade relationship with China; Darwin Port dispute.

basis.claim: Pentagon awarded first major AUKUS submarine contract ($276m).
China's ambassador warned Australia against forced Darwin Port buyback, hinting at sanctions.
Premier Li Qiang urged Albanese to speed China-Australia FTA review and expand trade.
US-Australia critical minerals framework signed, up to US$8.5bn pipeline to counter China.

CA.name: Canada
CA.summary: Open trade war with US after talks collapsed; diversifying via China tariff reset and Europe.

basis.claim: Canada's dollar-for-dollar counter-tariffs (15-50%) on $20bn US goods took effect; no active talks.
US 50% tariffs on ~$20bn Canadian goods took effect under Section 338 after talks collapsed.
Carney-Xi deal: Canada admits 49,000 Chinese EVs at 6.1%; China cuts canola tariffs.

BR.name: Brazil
BR.summary: Lula re-elected; tariff dispute with US easing but unresolved; minerals open to all incl. China; EU-Mercosur deal in force provisionally.

basis.claim: Lula won fourth term; Brazil awaits written US tariff proposal on remaining duties.
Lula said Brazil cannot accept new US Section 301 tariff proposals.
Lula-Trump White House meeting eased tensions; Lula insisted rare-earth investment open to China too.
EU-Mercosur interim trade agreement entered provisional application.

MX.name: Mexico
MX.summary: Sheinbaum cooperates with US on security and trade (tariffs on Chinese goods) but rejects US troops; USMCA under annual review.

basis.claim: US declined to extend USMCA, opting for annual reviews; Mexico tariffs partly exempt for USMCA goods.
Mexico's tariffs up to 50% on 1,463 lines from non-FTA countries, mainly China, took effect.
Sheinbaum said US troop deployment in Mexico 'not on the table'.
Despite Trump's UN rhetoric, US-Mexico security cooperation continues.

CL.name: Chile
CL.summary: Kast government tilts to US on minerals and security while China remains top trade partner; joined Pax Silica.

basis.claim: Chile and US signed critical-minerals and security agreements in Santiago.
Chile among ten new signatories of US Pax Silica declaration.
Lithium tender awarded to Chinese state entity then cancelled; US revoked visas of ex-Boric officials.

CO.name: Colombia
CO.summary: Swung from Petro's clashes with Trump to pro-US de la Espriella government (from Aug 2026); still faces 12.5% US tariff.

basis.claim: De la Espriella took office pledging to rebuild US ties, reversing Petro policies.
US sanctioned President Petro and family over drug-trade accusations.
Colombia placed in 12.5% tier of US Section 301 tariffs.

PE.name: Peru
PE.summary: Fujimori government (from July 2026) courted by US on security; Chinese-owned Chancay port a live issue.

basis.claim: Keiko Fujimori inaugurated; expected to intensify US push to draw Peru away from Beijing.
US pressed Peru on security and China; COSCO holds 60% of Chancay port.

EU.name: European Union
EU.summary: Implemented the 15% tariff deal with the US despite Greenland threats; delayed parts of the AI Act; manages Chinese rare-earth leverage through a fast-track licence arrangement.

basis.claim: EU-China trade talks in Beijing: China keeps a fast-track for rare-earth/magnet licences; the controls themselves are not lifted.
Digital Omnibus in force: AI Act high-risk (Annex III) obligations delayed from Aug 2026 to Dec 2027.
EU-US trade deal in force: EU drops tariffs on US industrial goods; US tariffs on EU goods capped at 15%.
EU signed the US-led Pax Silica tech supply-chain declaration at the second summit.
MEPs approved the US deal after weeks of resistance over Greenland threats and new US tariffs.

UK.name: United Kingdom
UK.summary: Close to the US but under trade pressure (Tech Prosperity Deal paused, digital-tax threats); pragmatic reset with China, including approval of the London mega-embassy.

basis.claim: Trump threatened a 'big tariff' unless the UK scraps its 2% digital services tax (date inferred from the article URL).
Starmer visited Beijing (Jan 28-31), the first UK PM visit since 2018; visa-free entry for UK travellers announced.
UK approved China's mega-embassy in London despite espionage concerns.
US paused the UK-US Tech Prosperity Deal (AI, quantum, nuclear) over digital tax, online safety and food rules.

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.summary: Squeezed between the US and China: seized control of Nexperia, faces US pressure to cut ASML's China sales further, and is now seeking to de-escalate with Beijing.

basis.claim: US reportedly preparing to press the Netherlands for a near-total ban on ASML sales and servicing in China.
Trade minister Sjoerdsma visited Beijing, the first such visit since 2018, seeking to move past the Nexperia dispute.
Netherlands signed the US-led Pax Silica declaration.
Wingtech, Nexperia's Chinese owner, is seeking about $8bn from the Netherlands over the government takeover.

DE.name: Germany
DE.summary: Still US-aligned (joined Pax Silica) despite US troop cuts and higher car tariffs; Merz's pragmatic re-engagement with Beijing has dropped the 'systemic rival' language.

basis.claim: Germany signed the Pax Silica declaration at the Washington summit.
US ordered a 5,000-troop withdrawal from Germany and raised EU car tariffs from 15% to 25% after Merz criticised the Iran war.
Merz played down the rift with Washington.
Merz's first China visit with 30 CEOs: Xi called for 'reliable partners'; Merz urged fewer market distortions.

BE.name: Belgium
BE.summary: Hawkish on China's economic impact, cool toward Trump after Greenland ('not slaves'), and the main holdout in the EU on using frozen Russian assets at Euroclear.

basis.claim: PM De Wever still demands full EU risk-sharing before any use of the ~EUR185bn in Russian assets at Euroclear.
De Wever said European leaders are 'increasingly wary' of China; Beijing's state media hit back.
De Wever wrote to the Commission that China is damaging the European economy.
De Wever told parliament that Europe is 'not slaves' of the US, amid the Greenland tensions.

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.summary: Neutral hedger moving closer to the EU (Bilaterals III signed) after a damaging US tariff saga: 39%, then 15%, then a Section 301 regime.

basis.claim: A US Section 301 duty applies to Swiss imports from 24 July 2026; SECO puts the total at 12.5%.
Switzerland and the EU signed the bilateral agreements package; it now goes to the Swiss parliament.
US agreed to cut tariffs on Swiss goods from 39% to 15%; Switzerland pledged $200bn of US investment.

DK.name: Denmark
DK.summary: Hit hardest by Trump's Greenland push; defused it with a September 2026 trilateral security deal that expands US access without ceding sovereignty. Relations remain wary.

basis.claim: The US, Denmark and Greenland signed a security deal expanding the US military footprint while keeping the island Danish.
Frederiksen formed a centre-left minority government amid the ongoing Greenland crisis with the US.
Denmark sent more troops to Greenland as Trump threatened tariffs on European countries deploying there.

FI.name: Finland
FI.summary: Front-line NATO state focused on Russia (drone incursions, border restrictions); joined the US Pax Silica tech bloc; cautious toward China.

basis.claim: Finland restricted air and sea traffic in the eastern Gulf of Finland amid stray drones from the Russia-Ukraine war.
Finland signed the Pax Silica declaration.
Nordic-Baltic foreign ministers jointly rejected Russian airspace accusations and condemned Russian threats against Latvia.

IS.name: Iceland
IS.summary: Voters narrowly rejected reopening EU accession talks; the government is still seeking closer security ties with the EU, under the shadow of Trump's Greenland threats.

basis.claim: Referendum rejected resuming EU accession talks, 52.8% to 47.2%.
Foreign minister said Iceland will still deepen security ties with the EU; vote held under the shadow of the Greenland threats.
Iceland joined the Nordic-Baltic statement condemning Russian threats over airspace incidents.

NO.name: Norway
NO.summary: NATO ally that joined Pax Silica; keeps trade with China (new seafood protocol) open while calling China a growing security threat.

basis.claim: Norway and China signed a seafood market-access protocol.
Wang Yi in Oslo; FM Eide said China poses a growing security threat to Norway; Støre raised China's support for Russia.
Norway signed the Pax Silica declaration.
Chinese embassy rejected Norway's 2026 threat assessment as a 'China threat narrative'.

SE.name: Sweden
SE.summary: Joined Pax Silica and names China among its top security threats, but began a cautious diplomatic reset with Beijing in July 2026.

basis.claim: Wang Yi met PM Kristersson in Stockholm; both sides spoke of rebuilding trust after years of setbacks.
Swedish security service named Russia, China and Iran as the main threats.
Sweden signed the Pax Silica declaration.

EE.name: Estonia
EE.summary: Russia hawk pushing tougher sanctions; presses China to stop supplying Russia's war economy; a drone was shot down over Estonia in May 2026.

basis.claim: FM Tsahkna urged Europe to keep pressure and tougher sanctions on Russia.
A NATO Baltic air-policing F-16 shot down a drone over Estonia, a first for the mission.
Tsahkna said China and North Korea may be the next Putin allies to fall.
Tsahkna in Beijing pressed Wang Yi to end support for Russia and dual-use exports.

CZ.name: Czech Republic
CZ.summary: The Babiš government is sceptical of the EU and Ukraine aid (opted out of the Ukraine loan costs) and is making cautious, pragmatic moves toward China.

basis.claim: Babiš argued Europe should redirect war funding to Ukraine's reconstruction.
Analysis: pragmatic tilt to China; in April Babiš refused a government plane for the Senate speaker's Taiwan trip.
Prague joined Slovakia and Hungary in opting out of the costs of the EU loan to Ukraine.

PL.name: Poland
PL.summary: Washington's favoured European ally: invited to the US-hosted 2026 G20, with the US pushing for permanent membership. Poland opposes Putin's G20 invitation.

basis.claim: Rubio praised Poland ahead of the Miami G20; the US is proposing permanent G20 membership for Poland.
Nawrocki will attend the Dec 14-15 Miami G20 despite protesting Putin's invitation.
Rubio announced Poland would be invited to the 2026 G20.

SA.name: Saudi Arabia
SA.summary: Deep US security and AI alignment (Strategic Defense Agreement, F-35 sale, Nvidia chips for Humain) while using Chinese software, cloud and telecoms.

basis.claim: Trump administration advanced a $24.3bn sale of 48 F-35s to Saudi Arabia.
Humain launched an Arabic AI model built on China's MiniMax, but pledged no Chinese frontier training on US-chip compute.
Commerce authorised exports of up to 35,000 GB300-equivalents each to Humain and G42.
Saudi Arabia designated a Major Non-NATO Ally; Strategic Defense Agreement signed.

AE.name: United Arab Emirates
AE.summary: The closest US AI partner in the Gulf: moved into the A:5 export tier with licence-free advanced chips, a Pax Silica signatory, and hit by Iranian strikes during the Iran war.

basis.claim: BIS moved the UAE to Country Group A:5; approved entities get licence-free advanced AI chips.
Iranian counterstrikes hit sites in the UAE and Bahrain after US-Israeli strikes began on Feb 28.
UAE signed the Pax Silica declaration.

QA.name: Qatar
QA.summary: Hosts Al Udeid and has pledged large US investments; a Pax Silica signatory; mediates DRC-M23 talks; came under Iranian fire during the 2026 Iran war.

basis.claim: US approved a $4.5bn refuelling-aircraft sale to Qatar; Qatar faces a 12.5% US tariff from July (secondary source).
IRGC claimed attacks on US assets in Qatar and other Gulf states as US strikes resumed.
Qatar became an early Pax Silica signatory.
Seventh US-Qatar Strategic Dialogue reaffirmed the defence partnership.

TR.name: Türkiye
TR.summary: Balancing: warmer with Trump (sanctions relief and F-35 talk) while flirting with the SCO; its bid to join the EU SAFE defence fund is blocked by Greece.

basis.claim: Commission reviewing Türkiye's request to join the EUR150bn SAFE fund; Greece is threatening a veto.
Erdogan demanded concrete steps on Türkiye's return to the F-35 programme.
At the Ankara NATO summit, Trump said the US will lift sanctions on Türkiye and consider F-35 sales.

CD.name: DR Congo
CD.summary: Trading minerals access for US security backing (Washington Accords, strategic minerals partnership); China still dominates its mining; war with Rwanda-backed M23 unresolved.

basis.claim: DRC and M23 agreed a roadmap for Doha-framework talks after meetings in Switzerland.
Glencore signed an MOU with the US-backed Orion consortium for a potential $9bn, 40% stake in DRC copper-cobalt assets.
Washington Accords signed with Rwanda, including a US-DRC strategic minerals partnership.

KE.name: Kenya
KE.summary: Openly multi-aligned: finalised a duty-free trade deal with China while negotiating US trade and critical-minerals deals. Ruto says Kenya won't choose sides.

basis.claim: Ruto said Kenya is close to a critical-minerals deal with the US, with processing to happen in Kenya.
Kenya finalised a trade deal with China giving duty-free access for 98% of its exports.
Kenya-China trade deal had reportedly been stalled by US pressure linked to AGOA.

NG.name: Nigeria
NG.summary: Turned Trump's threats over the killing of Christians into limited security cooperation, but faces US visa curbs and religious-freedom pressure; financial ties with China remain steady.

basis.claim: US ended routine visa services in Abuja; partial visa suspension in force since Jan 1, 2026.
Nigeria turned US threats into a military partnership; about 200 US personnel deployed (withdrawn June 2026).
US strikes in Sokoto State carried out in coordination with Nigeria.
Tinubu asked China to enlarge the $2bn naira-yuan currency swap; Wang Yi welcomed Nigeria to BRICS.

RW.name: Rwanda
RW.summary: Under escalating US sanctions (army in March, defence ministry in October 2026) for backing M23 in violation of the Washington Accords. Kagame is defiant.

basis.claim: Treasury sanctioned Rwanda's Ministry of Defense and Zigama Credit and Savings Society over M23 financing.
Kagame said US sanctions won't weaken Rwanda's defence forces.
Treasury sanctioned the Rwanda Defence Force and four senior officers over Washington Accords violations.
European Parliament voted to suspend the EU-Rwanda raw-materials memorandum (date approximate).

ZA.name: South Africa
ZA.summary: Frozen out of the US-hosted G20 and hit by aid cuts and visa curbs; deepening trade with China under Beijing's zero-tariff scheme.

basis.claim: SA-China trade rose ~24% year on year (May-Aug) after China's zero-tariff access took effect.
South Africa confirmed it is stepping back from G20 engagement during the US presidency.
Trump administration said South Africa will not be invited to the 2026 G20 in Miami.
China granted South Africa zero-tariff access on 100% of tariff lines.

caveats: US self-score toUS=2 and China self-score toChina=2 are placeholders; ignore for self-relations.
To Lam China visit date given as 2026-04-14 is approximate (mid-April 2026, four-day visit); exact start day UNVERIFIED.
US-China truce extension to Jan 10, 2027 announced by US; as of late Oct 2026 matching legal texts reportedly unpublished; Chinese rare-earth suspension legally lapses Nov 10 absent new notice.
US-India: 18% rate announced Feb 2026 reportedly never implemented; whether tariffs under the Sept 2026 Russia sanctions law have been applied to India is UNVERIFIED.
Canada-US: no October 2026 developments found; status after Sept 8 retaliation UNVERIFIED.
Brazil: whether the 2025 40% tariff layer is fully removed is UNVERIFIED; reports cite remaining 25%/37.5% duties on ~US$10.8bn exports.
Malaysia Huawei Ascend decision and ratification of US-Malaysia trade pact: UNVERIFIED as of Oct 2026.
Singapore's exact US tariff rate conflicts across sources (10%/15%/12.5%); EY lists 12.5% Section 301 tier.
Thailand: outcome of Feb 2026 election not checked; Anutin reported as PM in Oct 2026.
China-Japan: no evidence found of easing of seafood ban, flight cuts or dual-use controls by Oct 2026; Takaichi APEC Shenzhen attendance (Nov 18-19) pending.
Section 232 chip tariff relief for Korea/Japan: outcome UNVERIFIED.

UAE licence-free AI chip easing (reported July 10, 2026) UNVERIFIED; Nov 2025 Commerce approvals for G42/Humain verified (commerce.gov/node/7216). Gulf deals are outside the 18-country list so not scored.
Some sources are secondary/aggregator sites (Rio Times, Latin Times, tech-insider.org, ground.news); key claims cross-checked where possible but treat their details cautiously.

EU scores are judgement calls from limited 2026 evidence (EU-India FTA, EU-Mercosur provisional application, EU-China preliminary deal Oct 2026); EU-Indonesia/Vietnam/Thailand ties not separately verified.
Colombia: de la Espriella request to suspend US tariffs after earthquake — outcome UNVERIFIED.
Many search summaries came from an AI-assisted search tool; only a subset of URLs (CNBC Xi summit, NBC Canada, EY Section 301) were fetched directly.

Research was done via web search on 2026-11-01. Most 2026 claims rest on secondary news reports. Only the BIS UAE release (2026-07-10) and the HRW Rwanda sanctions article (2026-10-30) were fetched and read directly.

Pax Silica: the June 2026 summit date is given as 2026-06-15 as an approximation (sources say 'June'). Individual join dates for QA/AE/SE/FI/NO come from Wikipedia. UK membership in Pax Silica was not verified, so it is not used.
UK-US: no confirmed status for the Tech Prosperity Deal after its December 2025 pause. The April 2026 digital-tax tariff threat is dated from a URL slug only (UNVERIFIED exact date).
